purpose.summary: Correct ONE defect in lightweight_pcste_efficiency_v1: its latency and throughput timed paths never entered torch.inference_mode(), although its frozen plan states that mode. This run re-measures CPU/GPU batch-1 latency and batch-32 throughput with inference mode actually active and verified.

defect.statement: torch.inference_mode() was intended for every timed inference (EFFICIENCY_BENCHMARK_PLAN.json measurement.mode = 'torch.inference_mode(), model .eval()') but was absent from the timed code path.

where_missing.detail: calls builders[fam]() via _time_loop(line 141); neither the closure (bench_common.model_only_fn line 229 / end_to_end_fn line 205) nor _time_loop establishes any grad context, so autograd graph construction was active during every timed forward
inline fn() timed via _time_loop with no grad context

where_present_and_correct.detail: both the warm-up forwards and the measured forward are wrapped

unaffected_measurements: parameter counts (param_report line 43 performs no forward)
serialized model size (torch.save byte measurement, no forward)
FLOPs (flop_report wraps its forward in inference mode)
GPU peak memory (memory_stage wraps both warm-up and measured forwards)
defect.expected_direction: absolute latency should FALL; ratios are expected to be approximately preserved because the omission applied identically to both models, but this is measured, not assumed

inputs.source: the same deterministic VALIDATION windows as efficiency_v1, verified field-by-field

scopes.model_only: prepared resident representation -> encoder -> dataset head -> logits
scopes.end_to_end: resident raw 1 s waveform -> stft_rep -> N2b normalisation -> collate -> encoder -> head -> logits
scopes.disk_io: excluded from both; waveform resident and normaliser lru_cache warmed before timing

held_identical_to_original.timing_method: time.perf_counter, with torch.cuda.synchronize() bounding each timed GPU region (the original convention, preserved; CUDA events are not substituted)
held_identical_to_original.interleaving: ABAB - within each dataset and scope, rounds alternate Full-S1/K1; even rounds A,B and odd rounds B,A. The realised order is written to order_log_*.json.

aggregation.primary: equal-domain mean of the four per-dataset medians

held_identical_to_original.rerun_policy: No valid run is repeated because a speed-up is smaller than expected. Only an infrastructure-invalid run may be repeated, with the reason recorded.

the_correction.change: the entire warm-up + timed region of both latency and throughput now executes inside 'with torch.inference_mode():'
the_correction.verification: torch.is_inference_mode_enabled() is asserted inside the timed loop at the first, last and every 100th sample, plus once before warm-up
the_correction.fail_closed: a false assertion raises InferenceModeViolation and aborts the run; the assertion tally and violation count are written to inference_mode_verification_*.json
the_correction.eval_mode: models are additionally asserted to be in .eval() before timing

cpu_throughput.deviation_reason: efficiency_v1 measured batch-32 throughput on GPU only. CPU batch-32 is added here because the same infrastructure supports it symmetrically for both models, but each CPU batch-32 sample takes seconds, so a reduced schedule is used. Each sample already aggregates 32 windows. The reduced schedule is recorded rather than presented as equal to the batch-1 schedule.
cpu_throughput.include_only_if: both models complete cleanly at the identical batch size

not_recomputed.rationale: unaffected by the defect and remain frozen; referenced from artifacts, never re-measured or hand-copied

q8_relationship.note: The Q8 extension already measured K1 FP32 vs Q8 with inference mode active and remains frozen. Any Full-S1 -> Q8 figure must be a clearly labelled chained ratio; direct cross-run division is not permitted unless timing conditions are demonstrably identical.

hardware.gpu_query: NVIDIA RTX 4000 Ada Generation, 580.126.09, 20475 MiB, P8, Enabled, 3105 MHz, 130.00 W

prohibitions_observed: no modification of frozen predictive results
no modification of the dissertation repository
no deletion or rewrite of historical benchmark files
